subject: Post-incident: sentinel token-store reconciliation summary
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Harvest Bank Security <security@harvestbank.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Mar 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-incident: sentinel token-store reconciliation summary

Hi Andrew / Harvest security team,

We completed our reconciliations this morning against the token-store shard sets that were implicated during Thursday's incident. Summary of what we did: 
- Performed a checksum sweep across all token-store shards (v2 layout) and compared against the live KV manifests.
- Ran an egress telemetry filter for the incident window (2028-03-08T21:10:00Z to 2028-03-08T21:42:00Z) and validated outgoing network flows tied to inference pods.
- Sampled 1,200 request payloads (stratified by customer_id and region) for PII and account identifiers; sampling criteria and index in attached manifest.

Findings (short):
- Checksums: matched for 99.998% of keys; a small set (18 keys) had transient mismatch due to in-progress compaction; full hash reconciliation completed and included in tokenstore_checksums.txt.
- Egress: no external destinations were observed that were not part of normal model fetch/registry traffic; no uploads to unknown endpoints.
- Sampled payloads: no customer account numbers, SSNs, or other regulated identifiers were present in the sampled request bodies.

Attachments: sentinel_recon_manifest.csv (sampling index), tokenstore_checksums.txt (hash diffs & resolution notes), sampling-notes-20280309.pdf (methodology).

Next steps we suggest:
1) We can run a second, deeper sampling pass keyed to the specific model prefixes you asked about — would you like us to proceed?
2) If you want a signed hash manifest for your audit records we can generate one and share via the secure drive link below.

I'm happy to hop on a call later today if you'd like us to walk through the artifacts.

Thanks,
Chloe Martin
Senior Customer Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0194
From: Andrew Leslie <andrew.leslie@harvestbank.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Mar 2028 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-incident: sentinel token-store reconciliation summary

Chloe,

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear summary. A couple of follow-ups from our side: 
- Can you confirm whether the 18 keys with transient mismatch were customer-scoped keys versus system metadata? We need that for our audit log entry.
- For the egress check: did you observe any writes to external object storage (S3/GCS) outside of redact-preserving uploads? Our security controls flagged a small spike in PUTs during the incident window and we'd like to cross-check.

If possible, please include a sha256-signed manifest for the final reconciled state so our internal auditors can verify the checksums without transferring the raw CSV.

Andrew Leslie
Director, Information Security
Harvest Bank
andrew.leslie@harvestbank.com
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Andrew Leslie <andrew.leslie@harvestbank.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Mar 2028 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-incident: sentinel token-store reconciliation summary

Andrew —

Quick answers inline and attaching the signed manifest per your request.

- The 18 mismatches: all were system housekeeping keys (compaction indexes & temporary compaction tombstones) and not customer-scoped data. I've marked them in tokenstore_checksums.txt with a flag "SYSTEM_KEY" and included the reconciliation timestamp (2028-03-09T02:03:17Z).
- External writes: the spike you saw correlates to a batch model artifact sync to our model-registry S3 bucket (registry.redwood-models, us-west-2) tied to a background promotion job. Those PUTs were to our private registry and carried no customer payloads; we captured the flow records and included the object keys in the manifest. No writes to customer-owned buckets or unknown third-party endpoints were observed.

Attachments included: 
- tokenstore_checksums.txt (with SYSTEM_KEY annotations and sha256 manifests),
- sentinel_recon_manifest.csv (sampling indices),
- sampling-notes-20280309.pdf (full methodology).
- Also pushed signed-manifest.sha256 to the secure Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/fakeid/sentinel-reconciliation-20280309 (permission: view, link shared to Harvest Security).

If you'd like the signed manifest notarized with a redwood-signer certificate we can arrange that via our security integrations team; I can loop in Dylan if you want a rotation of the signing key.

Let me know if you'd like us to run the deeper model-prefix keyed sampling — we can start that pass tonight and share results tomorrow morning.

Regards,
Chloe

Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Mar 2028 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-incident: sentinel token-store reconciliation summary

Andrew —

Thanks for the follow-ups. Per Chloe's notes: the mismatches were system keys only and the PUT spike is accounted for by an internal model-registry sync. Harvest Security's request for a sha256-signed manifest has been satisfied; Chloe pushed the file to the secure drive link and I've added a Jira entry (INF-4721) with the manifest ID for your auditors to reference.

Action items we will track for closure: 
- Chloe to run model-prefix keyed sampling tonight and deliver results by 2028-03-10 09:00 PT (owner: chloe.martin).
- Dylan to coordinate an optional notarized signature if Harvest wants a signer certificate (owner: dylan.brooks).
- Laura to attach the drive manifest to Jira INF-4721 and mark the evidence package as "deliverable to customer auditors".

If that timeline works for you, we'll mark the incident as closed for data-integrity/integrity-of-logs concerns and continue monitoring.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Trust Operations
Redwood Inference
